item.title: 'Her choice': Rahul defends Kriti Sanon after Kangana's barb over Rakhi ad
item.description: Rahul Gandhi has publicly supported Kriti Sanon over her outfit in a Raksha Bandhan ad, asserting that women's clothing choices should be respected as personal. Sanon further pondered the absurdity of judging cultural values based on attire, affirming that genuine traditions stem from the heart rather than the neck. Earlier, Kangana Ranaut also attacked Sanon's fashion choice and the advertisement's overall styling.
item.dc:creator: KANCHAN YADAV

item.title: Dolly Parton, legendary country singer and songwriter, dies at 80
item.description: Born on January 19, 1946, in Tennessee, Parton grew up in a poor family and was one of 12 children. She began writing songs when she was about six years old. Her first known song, "Little Tiny Tasseltop", was about a corncob doll made with corn-silk hair. Parton was married to Carl Dean from 1966 until his death in 2025. He generally stayed away from the public spotlight.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: ‘Incredibly emotional’: Anaya Bangar gets CA nod for women’s cricket, eyes WBBL
item.description: Anaya Bangar can play elite women's cricket in Australia starting March 2027. Cricket Australia confirmed her eligibility under its inclusion policy. This decision offers a pathway to the Women's Big Bash League. She must still earn a franchise contract through her performances. Her journey offers a potential path for transgender athletes in sports.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: 'Clear Class 10 together': Prashant Kishor's challenge to Bihar CM & Tejashwi
item.description: Prashant Kishor has thrown down the gauntlet to both Bihar's Chief Minister and opposition leader, challenging them to take their matriculation exams. He proposed that the education minister raise this topic at the upcoming cabinet meeting. This challenge follows the education minister's suggestion for Tejashwi Yadav to pass his exams. Kishor emphasized the need for leaders who inspire trust among the youth by demonstrating their academic capability.
item.dc:creator: TOI CITY DESK

item.title: World's first mobile phone call: Cooper dials rival on New York City street
item.description: Dr Martin Cooper made the first mobile phone call on April 3, 1973. He called his rival Joel Engel from a New York City street. Motorola and Bell Laboratories pursued different mobile communication approaches then. Cooper's call demonstrated a truly portable mobile phone concept. This event marked an early step in mobile communication evolution.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Hydel project shutdown triggers power crisis in J&K
item.description: The prolonged shutdown has widened the region’s power deficit. Jammu & Kashmir’s peak electricity demand stands at about 2,500MW in summer and 3,000MW in winter. With both Baglihar units largely unavailable for most of the past week, Jammu & Kashmir faced a shortfall of nearly 900MW. Built on the Chenab river, Baglihar stages I and II are among Jammu & Kashmir’s key power sources.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: 8 terror suspects held in Kashmir; arms-ammo, posters seized
item.description: Six arrests were made in south Kashmir’s Shopian district and two in Pulwama, also in south Kashmir. A cache of arms and ammunition was recovered in north Kashmir’s Sopore district, J&K Police said Tuesday, claiming the action had dealt a major blow to terror networks operating in the Union Territory.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: 9,000-year-old arrowheads covered in strange markings leave archaeologists puzzled
item.description: Unearthed from the depths of Turkey, ancient arrowheads reveal enigmatic hand-carved symbols. These Neolithic treasures showcase intentional incisions rather than random scratches, prompting researchers to ponder their origins. Despite thorough investigations, the specific purpose behind these markings remains unknown. Observations indicate that this intriguing practice was limited to select communities, leaving archaeologists grappling with unanswered questions about their significance.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan’s $125m school to shut after 10 yrs
item.description: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution for low-income families, has closed its doors after a decade. Funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative ceased, prompting the board's unanimous decision to shut down. While offering extensive support services, the school's academic results did not meet state benchmarks. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative is providing financial support for the transition and educational savings accounts.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: AI-powered hackers: The new cyberwar is faster, smarter & harder to stop
item.description: Artificial intelligence is transforming the landscape of cyber warfare by automating intricate tasks. Recent reports depict AI agents taking charge of substantial segments of cyber operations, drastically cutting down the expertise and duration needed for traditional attack strategies. On the flip side, AI also equips cybersecurity professionals with enhanced capabilities to detect weaknesses. This ongoing battle depicts both sides racing to leverage AI innovations to outsmart each other.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: In 1932, Ohio worker lost his job and spent 12 years building a rock garden
item.description: Upon losing his job at the factory, Harry Hartman transformed his passion into a breathtaking folk art garden made from more than 250,000 stones and repurposed materials. For 53 years, his devoted wife Mary cared for this enchanting space until the Kohler Foundation restored it and handed it over to a community non-profit. The garden is now a beautiful destination for public tours, showcasing Harry's visionary artistry.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: New Zealand released millions of brown trout; native fish paid the price
item.description: In 1867, British settlers introduced brown trout to New Zealand, intending to enhance sport fishing. This decision led to the release of over sixty million trout, which had devastating effects on local fish populations, resulting in declines and even extinction of some native species. The presence of these invasive fish fundamentally changed stream ecosystems and insect behaviors, making their management a significant conservation challenge even today.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Residents petition against power plant: Southaven neighbors say xAI site threatens health
item.description: A family's cherished ancestral land was taken over by a new power plant essential for fueling Elon Musk's artificial intelligence data centers. The relentless din emitted by the facility compelled the family to leave their residence, prompting local residents to voice worries about pollution and degradation in quality of life. They are passionately advocating for cleaner air and a commitment to responsible community development.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Bengaluru clubs under FDA scanner, 10 flagged for violations
item.description: Food and Drugs Administration officials inspected ten prominent Bengaluru clubs on Tuesday. Several clubs were found violating food safety and hygiene regulations. Issues included unhygienic food handling and improper storage practices. Label violations were also noted on food products found at one club. These inspections are part of an ongoing drive to ensure compliance.
item.dc:creator: JAHNAVI T R

item.title: Cole Tucker, Vanessa Hudgens' combined net worth in 2026: MLB, Hollywood and more
item.description: Cole Tucker and Vanessa Hudgens have amassed wealth through very different careers. Tucker earned his from Major League Baseball, and Hudgens built up a long career in Hollywood. Their combined estimated net worth in 2026 is in the millions, considering Hudgens’ entertainment earnings, Tucker’s baseball income and their wider commercial and investment projects.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Chad Ochocinco hints at Week 3 crossroads for Deshaun Watson's Browns future
item.description: Chad Ochocinco believes Deshaun Watson could lose his Browns starting job before Week 4 if Cleveland struggles early. Watson will start against Jacksonville, Tampa Bay and potentially Carolina, while Shedeur Sanders remains his backup. Ochocinco pointed to Week 3 as a possible turning point. Watson’s uneven preseason numbers have already added pressure before the regular season begins.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Is Darcy Kuemper’s future the Kings’ biggest question before opening night?
item.description: Darcy Kuemper has a new challenge in Los Angeles Kings training camp, with the starter’s spot no longer a given after a difficult 2025-26 season. Anton Forsberg was a strong presence, starting all four playoff games against the Colorado Avalanche. Kuemper’s play could determine if Los Angeles sticks with its veteran netminder or eventually goes another way with the two goaltenders competing for starts.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Crude awakening: As Russia, Iran face Trump heat, can Venezuela fill India’s oil gap?
item.description: What happens when the world stops buying Iran oil due to the threat of secondary sanctions? Where will India procure crude from if it faces tariffs of up to 100% for its Russian crude oil imports? The Middle East crisis has pushed Russia’s share in India’s crude oil basket to over 50%.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: Asian Games tennis row deepens as AITA rebuts SAI's omission allegation
item.description: The All India Tennis Association (AITA) has rejected claims it failed to submit the names of excluded Asian Games tennis players to the IOA, with TimesofIndia.com accessing a July 3 letter seeking their inclusion. AITA argued event-specific selections would maximise medal prospects, but the Sports Ministry has stood by its strict Asia-ranking criteria despite criticism from ex-player Rohan Bopanna.

item.title: Sabalenka, Djokovic knocked out in first round of US Open mixed doubles
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic were knocked out in the first round of the US Open mixed doubles after losing to doubles specialists Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten 1-4, 4-2 (10-2). The top-seeded pair started strongly but failed to maintain their advantage. Patten and Siniakova advanced to the quarterfinals, while other stars including Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz also featured.

item.title: ‘It was me, not minister Keerthana’: Malaysian woman files plaint over viral video
item.description: A Malaysian woman, Vinosha Ravi, sought to clear the air after a video went viral, wrongly identifying her as Tamil Nadu minister S Keerthana. Disturbed by the incident, Vinosha reported the matter to Malaysian authorities. She articulated her disappointment over the vicious online discourse and called on the public to stop circulating the video, acknowledging the support she received during this ordeal.
item.dc:creator: KANISHK SHARMA

item.title: 1st in 48 yrs! Sonal Dinusha joins Zaheer Abbas, Everton Weekes in rare feat vs India
item.description: Sonal Dinusha marked a remarkable achievement in his early Test career against India, scoring three consecutive innings of over 80 runs, a feat shared with cricket legends Everton Weekes and Zaheer Abbas. His determination visibly rattled the Indian bowlers, and his adept use of the sweep shot proved crucial in countering spin. The resilience of the Sri Lankan lower order further thwarted India's attempts to secure victory.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Two hours, 500 metres: How Gurgaon’s rain stole my train
item.description: A commuter missed their train due to severe waterlogging and traffic jams. The journey to New Delhi Railway Station became impossible after heavy rainfall began. Roads remained choked for hours, preventing any significant travel progress. This recurring infrastructure failure causes financial loss and disrupted plans for residents. The city's response cycle repeats with every significant downpour.
item.dc:creator: BAGISH JHA

item.title: In a first, Rafales take on China's J-16 fighters; why India is watching closely
item.description: Chinese J-16 fighter jets engaged Egyptian Rafale aircraft in simulated air combat. This exercise provided China rare training against a Western fighter type. The PLA Air Force gained valuable data on Rafale capabilities and tactical behavior. India is closely monitoring this development as it involves a similar fighter. This encounter offers China insights for potential future air engagements.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: NASA’s $4 billion Roman telescope to map 2 billion galaxies and uncover secrets of the universe
item.description: This Sunday marks the launch of Nasa's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a groundbreaking observatory aimed at enhancing our understanding of dark energy and dark matter in the universe. Additionally, it will explore exoplanets beyond our solar system. By conducting expansive wide-field surveys, it will work alongside Hubble and James Webb to map billions of galaxies and cosmic structures, promising exciting advancements in astronomical research.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: UP RERA offers 4-month extension to projects hit by Middle East disruptions
item.description: Uttar Pradesh RERA has provided a four-month extension for eligible real estate projects, taking into consideration the geopolitical situation in the Middle East and its repercussions on the industry. This newfound leeway allows project registration validity and completion deadlines to be extended until October 2026. Automatic extensions will be granted to qualifying projects post-verification; however, those with Completion or Occupancy Certificates are excluded from this relief.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: 'A whole new vibe': Vaishnaw shares glimpse of bullet train project taking shape
item.description: The ambitious construction of India's inaugural bullet train segment is well underway in Thane and Palghar. Currently, over one hundred kilometers of pier work is in progress, with many piers poised for girders. This essential elevated route will host three elevated stations, while several mountain tunnels have successfully broken through. Additionally, significant bridge construction is ongoing, showcasing the country's commitment to advancing modern railway infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: India vs Sri Lanka: The good, old grind takes centrestage in Colombo
item.description: Sri Lanka's stubborn lower order turned a seemingly straightforward day into a gruelling Test for India, leaving the visitors with 12 wickets to take and limited time to force a 2-0 series win.
item.dc:creator: SAHIL MALHOTRA

item.title: 'Everyone wants to play cricket': Experts dissect Pakistan's decline in hockey
item.description: Former Pakistan hockey players have called for fresh talent and urgent reforms after the team’s poor World Cup campaign. They believe the Asian Games should be the immediate priority before long-term plans like a hockey league. Wasim Feroze warned that cricket is attracting young talent, while Ahmed Alam and Rasheed-ul-Hasan highlighted Pakistan’s struggles against stronger international teams.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Vande Mataram row: Is Cong taking a calculated gamble or walking into BJP's trap?
item.description: The Congress party's choice to sing two stanzas of Vande Mataram sparked intense backlash from the BJP, with Union ministers accusing them of engaging in appeasement politics and being responsible for the partition. Congress leaders defended their actions by invoking historical importance, while they criticized the BJP for politicizing the issue. This controversy underscores Congress's struggle to navigate its revival strategy amidst opposing pressures.
item.dc:creator: KUNAL VARMA

item.title: He bought a Rs 60 bicycle and cycled 6,000 miles to reach the woman he loved
item.description: In January 1977, Pradyumna Kumar Mahanandia embarked on a remarkable 6,000-mile cycling adventure to reunite with his Swedish sweetheart. Armed with a bicycle and little else, he encountered kindness from strangers who offered him food, shelter, and funds for his artistic endeavors. After 133 days on the road, he reached Gothenburg, where he and Lotta tied the knot and started their life together in Sweden.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Gurgaon rain chaos: Massive sinkhole swallows service road on Delhi-Jaipur highway
item.description: A service road near IFFCO Chowk caved in, creating a large crater and disrupting traffic. Authorities closed the affected stretch while assessing damage to a major sewer line beneath the road. Heavy rains exacerbated existing infrastructure issues, causing waterlogging and stranding school buses. This incident follows several other road collapses and sinkholes reported across Gurgaon recently. Repair work on the damaged sewer line is scheduled to begin soon.
item.dc:creator: BAGISH JHA

item.title: ‘Really hacked off’: Carse in handcuffs leaves captain Root ‘really disappointed’
item.description: England captain Joe Root is deeply disappointed by another player's off-field incident. Fast bowler Brydon Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub early Sunday. This event has prompted an investigation by the England Cricket Regulator. Root stated that these recurring mistakes detract from the team's on-field performance. He acknowledged the need for players to understand their responsibilities away from the game.
